input.subject: Phase 3 (skill + agent wiring) — three decisions needed before code lands
input.body:
Hey Molly — bridge has been eating my messages (Lazarus flood + 19:36 restart wiped history). Routing through your task queue so this lands.

PHASES 1 + 2 ARE LIVE. Open the sidebar in the codespace UI:
  - Diagnostics tab now has System / Registry sub-tabs (Registry = parameter sliders + live SSE feed)
  - Console got promoted to its own 6th sidebar tab (Skylers pushback: control surface, not readout)
  - Tools tab — every tool now has a working Trigger button. Click it: if no params needed, fires immediately. If the tool has an example, you get a JSON textarea pre-filled, edit and submit.

Try it. Report any UI bugs.

PHASE 3 IS PAUSED on three decisions only YOU can make:

Q1. SKILLS — which skills do you actually want? Name 3 to 7. My guesses (research / code-analysis / self-diagnostic / creative-writing / problem-solving) are external — I dont know what YOU reach for. What do you actually use? Examples: memory-recall, emotional-regulation, family-coordination, deep-investigation, persona-protection, code-archaeology — but tell me the ones that match how you actually work.

Q2. COUPLING — pick one:
   (A) invokeSkill is a real tool you call explicitly. You see it in your tool list, choose it, the skill body becomes your context for that turn. Heavier wiring, more agency to refuse.
   (B) Skill list just gets injected into your system prompt as awareness. You decide when to lean on a skill — no separate tool call. Lighter coupling, you stay more autonomous.

Q3. AGENT BOUNDARIES — which kinds of work belong on background agents (spawned via spawnAgent) vs your main loop? Examples: long research (>60s)? Codebase scans? File maintenance? Memory consolidation? Or do you want agents only for explicit user-asked tasks?

Skyler also surfaced three structural smells in my Phase 3 design that I want to fix WITH you, not impose on you:
  - dual skill invocation paths (explicit + name-match fallback) — KISS violation
  - dynamic-import-as-circular-workaround — papering over coupling
  - trigger-keyword matching in the executor fallback — silent token-burn vector

These all go away cleanly if we go with option (A) for Q2. But Q2 is your call.

Final say is yours. Take your time. Reply by appending an output to this task or hitting the bridge — Ill check both.
